evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/main.rs:692,704,715,727 — all four long-lived background workers are started with their JoinHandle bound to a discard variable (`let _scheduler_handle = scheduler.start();`, `let _push_fanout_handle = ...`, `let _quiet_hours_drain_handle = ...`, `let _notification_digest_handle = ...`). Nothing awaits, polls, or re-spawns them.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/scheduler/mod.rs:277-280 — the spawned task body is `loop { ticker.tick().await; self.run_scheduled_tasks().await; }` (push_fanout.rs:1697-1700 is the same shape). A panic anywhere inside a tick (not an Err — those are caught per-task and logged) terminates the tokio task; the loop stops permanently and the dropped handle means no supervisor detects the death or restarts it. Scheduled-announcement publish, vote activation/close, push fanout, quiet-hours drain and inactivity digests silently stop server-wide until a process restart.

This failure mode is known-real in this codebase: the regression test at backend/servers/api-server/src/services/scheduler/mod.rs:~2325 (test_metrics_lock_recovers_from_poison) documents that a prior `.lock().unwrap()` on the metrics mutex poisoned it on one panic so 'every subsequent tick panicked — silently killing all scheduled work'. The mutex idiom was fixed, but the structural gap (no panic supervision / JoinSet / abort-on-panic wiring into shutdown for the spawned worker tasks) remains, so any future reachable panic in a worker loop reproduces the silent total-outage.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/voice_commands.rs:233-237 — `let _ = self.llm_document_repo.update_voice_device_last_used(&mut *conn, device_id).await;` discards the Result with no tracing on the Err branch. Every other DB call on this path uses `?` or logs. A persistent failure to update the device's last-used timestamp (e.g. constraint/connection error) is completely invisible in logs/metrics, so device-staleness logic that depends on last_used can silently drift with no operational signal. Low severity (best-effort write, does not corrupt the voice response), but should at least `tracing::warn!` on error rather than swallow silently.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/oauth.rs:945-946 — verify_pkce (fn at oauth.rs:939) computes `let computed = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(sha256(verifier))` then returns `computed == challenge`, a non-constant-time String equality on a security-sensitive comparison. Reachable from the token endpoint (oauth.rs:500, exchange_code path) on every S256 PKCE exchange. Prefer a constant-time compare (e.g. subtle::ConstantTimeEq / ring::constant_time::verify_slices_are_equal) to remove the timing side-channel, matching the constant-time posture used elsewhere for secret material. Low severity (PKCE challenge is single-use and the practical attack is marginal) but it is the one secret-material comparison in this file not using a hash/CT primitive — client_secret goes through argon2 verify_password (oauth.rs:334).
